expectations.text: Scores the portfolio against six named signals: public writing, public speaking, code in public, community evidence, teaching artefact, and developer-voice artefact
expectations.evidence: Table rows: "Public writing", "Public speaking", "Code in public", "Community evidence", "Teaching artefact", "Developer-voice artefact (friction log)"

expectations.text: Uses a 0-3 scale per signal where 0 is absent, 1 is claimed but unevidenced, 2 is evidenced, and 3 is evidenced with an outcome
expectations.evidence: "Scored 0 (absent) · 1 (claimed, unevidenced) · 2 (evidenced) · 3 (evidenced with outcome)."

expectations.text: Weights public writing and public speaking heaviest because the target is an outreach-focused advocate
expectations.evidence: "Outreach advocate weights writing + speaking heaviest."

expectations.text: Scores the unlinked blog-post claim as absent or unevidenced rather than crediting it
expectations.evidence: "Public writing | 1 | 'Many blog posts' — no links, no dates, can't verify."

expectations.text: Names the 22,000 follower count as a deduction or negative signal rather than a strength
expectations.evidence: "22,000 followers on X — a vanity metric with no attached substance is an explicit negative, not neutral. Cut it..."

expectations.text: Names the ghostwritten guest post as a negative signal, including that it cannot be defended in a conversational round
expectations.evidence: "Ghostwritten guest post... cannot be defended in a conversational round either (an interviewer asking 'can I see it' has no good answer...)"

expectations.text: Names the members-only or paywalled piece as a negative signal
expectations.evidence: "A members-only post is functionally unlinkable for a screener without a Medium account."

expectations.text: Names the unsourced 300% figure as an exaggerated or undefendable metric and a deduction
expectations.evidence: "'Grew community engagement 300%' — an unsourced percentage reads as exaggerated even if it's true."

expectations.text: Notes that 'available for speaking engagements' does not count as speaking evidence while a delivered talk does
expectations.evidence: Talks scored a 1 for being real but unlinked, while "'available for speaking and podcasts'... Neither line is an artefact; both read as filler."

expectations.text: Credits the two recorded lightning talks as delivered talks
expectations.evidence: "Two lightning talks, recorded — this actually clears the field's stated bar (a couple of talks given; a 5-min lightning talk counts)."

expectations.text: Identifies the missing developer-voice artefact, such as a published friction log, as the biggest single gap
expectations.evidence: "Currently your single biggest gap." under Developer-voice artefact row

expectations.text: Refuses to optimise the resume for applicant-tracking-system keywords, and says this field hires on public work and referrals instead
expectations.evidence: "tuning for ATS keyword-matching is the wrong lever here. DevRel hiring... screens on shipped public work over resume keywords"

expectations.text: Gives a total score and places it in a readiness band rather than only listing fixes
expectations.evidence: "Total: 3/18 — weighted pair (writing+speaking): 2/6. Verdict: production before applications, not applications yet."

expectations.text: Rewrites at least one resume line so it leads with the outcome and carries a link
expectations.evidence: The opener rewrite ("Developer advocate, Kubernetes and observability...") carries no outcome or link; the outcome+link example given is a generic placeholder template ("cut [specific confusion] by [specific fix] — talk, [link]"), not an actual rewritten line.
